title: Cello Concerto in D major (Haydn)
description: Guilhermina Suggia, born in Porto in 1885, was one of the great cellists of her time, admired by Pablo Casals. Her 1928 recording of Haydn’s concerto is among the few she made. The main hall of the Casa da Música is named after her.

title: Chico Fininho
description: Rui Veloso’s first hit, with lyrics by Carlos Tê, about a skinny small-time hustler drifting around Porto’s downtown. Its success in 1980 started a boom in rock sung in Portuguese.

title: Dunas
description: GNR, a Porto band led by singer Rui Reininho, released this beach song as a single in 1985, and it became one of their best-known hits. The beaches just north of the city, at Matosinhos and Leça da Palmeira, are where Porto goes to the sea.

title: Porto Sentido
description: Rui Veloso and lyricist Carlos Tê’s love song to Porto, with its granite, river mist, and steep streets, has become the city’s unofficial anthem. The view from Miradouro da Vitória takes in the rooftops it describes.

title: Tudo o que eu te dou
description: The breakthrough of Pedro Abrunhosa, a Porto jazz musician turned pop star in dark glasses, from his first album, Viagens. The Coliseu, Porto’s 1941 Art Deco concert hall, is one of his regular stages.

title: Ouvi Dizer
description: The best-known song by Ornatos Violeta, a Porto band whose second album, O Monstro Precisa de Amigos, is often named the best Portuguese rock record of the 1990s. The band split up soon after.

title: O Amor É Mágico
description: A hit for Expensive Soul, a soul and hip-hop duo from Leça da Palmeira, the seaside town just north of Porto, made up of New Max and Demo.
